https://www.thedailybeast.com/putin-melt.text: World Putin Melts Down in Front of Stunned Sailors After Canceling Parade TALK THERAPY The Russian leader’s show of strength comes as his carefully managed image increasingly crumbles. Wiktoria Gucia Reporter Updated Jul. 26 2026 4:56PM EDT / Published Jul. 26 2026 4:50PM EDT Comments Vladimir Putin scrapped Russia’s Navy Day parade over fears of Ukrainian strikes and then raged to a group of sailors about a revenge fantasy and Soviet dictator Josef Stalin. After canceling the parade—which was set to feature around 200 warships sailing along the Neva River in St. Petersburg—the president opted for a televised meeting with Navy personnel. In an apparent bid to save face, he angrily predicted that Ukraine would ultimately fall apart, claiming that Russia had actually been the only “guarantor” of Ukraine’s “territorial integrity.” Apart from the eastern regions of Ukraine that Moscow has tried to claim as its own, Putin declared the western regions “a gift from Stalin” and claimed they would “sooner or later” return to Hungary, Romania, and Poland. The 73-year-old leader sounded somewhat defeated as he admitted that such a “return” would not happen immediately, suggesting it could take “a year, or two, or maybe even ten or fifteen” before everything would “historically fall into place.” Russian President Vladimir Putin visits the Main Admiralty to meet with commanders on Navy Day in Saint Petersburg, Russia, July 26, 2026. Vyacheslav Prokofyev/via REUTERS The claims about Ukraine’s western regions are a recurring part of the Kremlin’s bogus historical narrative that Putin has repeatedly used to try and justify his war. The move came as Putin’s war faces a growing backlash at home, with a months-long Ukrainian drone campaign targeting Russian oil infrastructure crippling parts of the country’s refining capacity, worsening fuel shortages, and stoking frustration among some of the Kremlin’s most loyal supporters. Putin Gets Spectacularly Ambushed After Leaving His Bunker DANGER ZONE Allison Quinn In a separate video address recorded from the safety of his office, Putin told sailors that Russia’s “naval forces are capable of effectively accomplishing the full range of tasks assigned to them.” The Russian leader also sought to project strength toward the West, boasting that the navy was “constantly developing,” including its nuclear strike capabilities. Putin’s display of confidence before Navy personnel, some of whom appeared less than convinced by his remarks, came just days after an uncomfortable public setback in which Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev used a meeting meant to highlight Russia-Kazakh ties to publicly undermine the Kremlin leader. Putin Left Out in the Cold as Trump Gushes Over New BFF SAD FOR VLAD Leigh Kimmins In remarks broadcast by state-controlled media, Tokayev said he had been receiving signals from both Europe and the United States about the war and had already discussed them with Putin. He then delivered a striking assessment, saying that “the nature of this conflict is not entirely clear,” which appeared to leave the Russian president visibly uncomfortable. The meltdown also comes amid growing frustration inside Russia, where Ukrainian strikes on warehouses belonging to Wildberries—the country’s equivalent of Amazon—have sparked anger among small business sellers as their financial losses pile up. Many sellers have expressed their frustration online. @fliginskikh/ Instagram “We’re already getting screwed over from every direction as it is,” cosmetic brand founder Svetlana Dodo said in an Instagram video , saying she had lost around 1 million rubles—about $12,800—after Ukrainian strikes set warehouses ablaze, destroying billions of dollars’ worth of inventory. Last Sunday, Vladimir Solovyov, one of Putin’s most prominent television propagandists, began his evening program by acknowledging that “things are difficult.” Putin, in comments to Russian sailors on Sunday, appeared to try and dismiss the growing public outrage that has begun to seep out online, claiming that it’s “dangerous” to rely on information in “online communities” because there is too much “clutter.” Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky claimed in a national address on Thursday that individuals close to Putin had contacted Kyiv and blamed the Russian leader personally for starting the war and the heavy losses Russia has suffered. https://nineoclock.ro/between-discipline.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Between Discipline and Calling: A Conversation with TAROM Boeing 737 First Officer George Ancuța, by Dr. Adrian Leonard Mociulschi Special for Nine O’Clock by Dr. Adrian Leonard Mociulschi For millions of passengers, a flight begins when the cabin doors close and the aircraft starts taxiing toward the runway. For the crew in the cockpit, however, every departure is preceded by a rigorous sequence of checks, calculations, and decisions designed to ensure the safety of the flight. On the occasion of Romanian Aviation Day , George Ancuța, a First Officer on TAROM’s Boeing 737 fleet, speaks about what passengers rarely see: the final minutes before takeoff, the challenges posed by adverse weather, the breathtaking views from cruising altitude, and the responsibility of carrying hundreds of people who place their trust in the flight crew. It is a conversation about discipline, preparation, and a profession that continues to inspire generations. Adrian Leonard Mociulschi: Many of our readers travel by air, yet few know what happens behind the cockpit door. What takes place in the cockpit during the final minutes before takeoff? George Ancu ța: The final minutes before takeoff are among the most important of the entire flight. Inside the cockpit, every member of the crew knows exactly what needs to be done, and our attention is fully focused on the final checks. We review the weather, aircraft performance data, the route, any operational restrictions, and ensure that all systems are functioning exactly as they should. There is a principle that guides every flight: prepare for the worst and hope for the best. That is why we discuss scenarios that are highly unlikely to occur. If something unexpected happens, we want to have a plan in place already and be able to respond quickly and effectively. All of these procedures are the result of rigorous training and teamwork. From the outside, it may seem like a routine stage before departure, but in the cockpit every check and every decision serves a single purpose: flight safety. Adrian Leonard Mociulschi: Flying is one of the few experiences that allows us to leave the routines of everyday life behind, if only for a few hours. Is there a particular moment during a flight that reminds you why you chose this profession? George Ancu ța: Yes. There are many special moments, but the ones that continue to impress me every single time are the sunsets seen from the cockpit. At cruising altitude, the colors of the sky are simply spectacular and unlike anything that can truly be captured in a photograph. Every sunset is different. Sometimes it feels as though you are flying through a painting. Those are moments of calm when you realize how privileged you are to see the world from a perspective that very few people ever experience. Whenever I watch one of those sunsets, I am reminded that I chose the profession I dreamed about as a child. Adrian Leonard Mociulschi: If there is a poetic side to flying, there is also another side where nature tests the experience and preparation of the crew. For passengers, turbulence may mean a few uncomfortable minutes. For pilots, it can be a moment when experience, training, and human judgment meet the forces of nature directly. What has been the most intense moment you have experienced in the cockpit? George Ancu ța: The most intense moments are always those when you have to confront nature. Thunderstorms, severe weather, or strong turbulence remind you that, no matter how advanced modern aircraft technology has become, nature must always be respected. In such situations, experience and preparation are essential. You remain calm, continuously evaluate the available information, and make the best decisions together with your colleague in the cockpit. Communication and trust between the two pilots are just as important as the aircraft itself. Paradoxically, these are also the moments that validate your training. Every hour spent in the simulator and every procedure practiced exists precisely for the moments when you need them most. Adrian Leonard Mociulschi: Romanian Aviation Day reminds us that every flight begins with a dream. What message would you like to share with young people who aspire to become airline pilots? George Ancu ța: I would tell them never to give up on their dream. I know how distant a cockpit can seem when you are standing on the ground, watching airplanes and imagining that one day you might be the one sitting up there. I was that child too. The road was not easy. There were years of study, examinations, sacrifices, and many challenges. But every step was worth it. If you have passion, discipline, and patience, the things that seem impossible today can become reality. For me, flying is much more than operating an aircraft. It means carrying the responsibility of having hundreds of people place their trust in you and your crew. It is a responsibility that I feel on every flight and, at the same time, a privilege that I will never take for granted. If a child who once watched airplanes with admiration can one day find himself in the cockpit of a Boeing 737, then I am convinced that other young people can turn their dreams into reality as well. The important thing is to believe in yourself and never give up. Adrian Leonard Mociulschi: Thank you very much, George, for your time and for this conversation. We wish you continued success, smooth flights, and clear skies. In Closing Romanian Aviation Day reminds us that behind every flight stand professionals for whom safety is not a statistic but a responsibility embraced every day. For passengers, flying is often simply a journey between two destinations. For those in the cockpit, it remains a mission built on discipline, competence, and trust. Through their professionalism and quiet dedication, Romania’s aviators continue to give meaning to a profession that inspires both respect and admiration. George Ancu ța is a First Officer flying the Boeing 737 for TAROM, Romania’s national airline. Adrian-Leonard Mociulschi is a contributor to Nine O’Clock, as well as a musician, essayist, and university lecturer at the National University of Music Bucharest (UNMB). His interdisciplinary work explores the symbolic intersections between music, emerging technologies, and cultural ethics. He is the author of five published essay volumes with Curtea Veche Publishing, a leading Romanian publishing house, and a regular contributor to Nine O’Clock and international academic journals. https://telex.hu/gazdasag/2026/09/22/eu-.text: Menü Kereső A magyar kormány is felsorolta, mit akar az EU következő hétéves költségvetésétől Gazdaság Márton Balázs Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Általánosságban egyetértenek, hogy év végéig meg kellene állapodni az Európai Unió következő hétéves költségvetésről – jelentette ki kedden az uniós ügyekkel foglalkozó miniszterek, államtitkárok ülése után Thomas Byrne. Az Európai Unió Tanácsának soros ír elnöksége nevében kijelentette: biztos benne, hogy tartani tudják a – nem hivatalos – határidőt. Az Európai Bizottság tavaly nyújtotta be a javaslatát a 2028-2034 közötti uniós költségvetésre. A kétezer milliárd eurós tervezet alaposan átalakítaná a rendszert, aminek az idén lejáró helyreállítási alap mögötti hitel visszafizetésével is számolnia kell. A kiadásoknál csökkenne a büdzsét jelenleg uraló felzárkóztatási és mezőgazdasági politika szerepe. A bevételeknél új saját forrásokat vezetnének be az eddig túlnyomórészt a bruttó nemzeti jövedelem (GNI) alapján összedobott pénz mellett. A keddi ülésen mindegyik tagállam képviselője, így Bíró-Nagy András államtitkár is felszólalt . (Hivatalosan csak néhány hete vette át a Miniszterelnökség európai uniós ügyeinek irányítását, de már korábban is képviselte Magyarországot a Tanácsban.) Közölte: a magyar kormányt inkább az alku minősége érdekli, nem az időzítése. Elsődlegesként tekint a felzárkóztatási és a mezőgazdasági politikára a kiadásoknál, és arra, hogy mekkora részt különítenek el Magyarországnak. Az előző, ciprusi elnökség nagyon jó kezdeti lépéseket tett, hogy megőrizze a felzárkóztatási alapot, utalt a júniusi tervezetre a költségvetés sarokszámairól. Attól tartott, hogy a tagállami kormányoknak túlságosan „fejnehéz” terveket kellene készíteniük, amiből forrásvesztés lehet. (A mostani rendszerben ráérnek akár a hétéves időszak végén is felpörgetni a pénzlehívást.) A forrásvesztésre szintén rugalmasabb szabályokat szeretne. (Az angolul általa emlegetett „decommitment”, ami összesen kétmilliárd euróval történt 2024 és 2025 végén , mert a mostani kormány elődje nem teljesített minden jogállami és korrupcióellenes előfeltételt, amelyet bevállalt.) Az Európai Bizottság országspecifikus ajánlásai politikailag sem lehetnek kötelezőek, utalt arra, hogy a testület az évente kiadott, a Tanács által jóváhagyott ajánlásaihoz köthető reformoktól tenné függővé a pénzlehívást, mint az idén lejáró, egyszeri helyreállítási alapnál . Arra panaszkodott, hogy Magyarországnak már a mostani költségvetési időszakban is a GNI-aránya felett kell befizetnie pénzt. A tervezett módosítások és új saját források „nem segítenek, hogy orvosolják ezt a helyzetet”. A GNI-re még jobban is támaszkodna a „megbízhatatlan” saját források helyett . Ezen a téren jelentős változásokat szeretnének az írek leendő tervezeténél a sarokszámokról, amelyet október közepe, a következő EU-csúcs előtt mutatnának be, közölte a magyar államtitkár. (Az állam- és kormányfők a tervek szerint decemberben is összeülnek.) A tagállami vezetőknek egyhangúlag kell megegyezniük a legfontosabb részleteket rögzítő sarokszámokról, és az Európai Parlament (EP) beleegyezésére is szükségük van. A Tanács keddi ülése után az EP-ből is külön közleménnyel jelezték az álláspontjukat . „Továbbra is meg fogjuk védeni, hogy a költségvetés megfelelő forrásokat biztosítson a hagyományos prioritásokra, a mezőgazdaságra és a felzárkóztatási politikára” az újak, például a biztonság és védelem mellett, üzente az EP egyik témafelelőse, Siegfried Mureşan. Társa, Carla Tavares arra figyelmeztetett: készen állnak rá, hogy dolgozzanak a beleegyezésükhöz szükséges feltételeken, de a „Tanácsnak is haladnia kell, különösen a valódi saját forrásokon”.
